newsitem.title: FRANCE: Embattled French premier to face live TV interview.
newsitem.headline: Embattled French premier to face live TV interview.

text.p: Embattled French Prime Minister Alain Juppe has agreed to take part in a live television interview next weekend, France's TF1 channel said on Sunday.
No subject was given for the interview on TF1's public affairs programme "7/7" at 7 p.m. (1700 GMT) on October 6.

But Juppe has come under fire, even from within his own centre-right coalition, over record joblessness, labour unrest and spending and job cuts intended to help France qualify to participate in a single European Union currency from 1999.

The sniping was so blatant at a recent conference of Juppe's Gaullist party that President Jacques Chirac telephoned a top party official to express his indignation and urge unity within the majority.
Juppe, speaking at a party conference in the Bordeaux region wine town of Saint-Emilion in southwestern France on Saturday, insisted that 95 percent of majority deputies were faithful supporters.

"And then there are one or two big-mouths," he added. "Well, we have set the record straight, and now things are fine. And I am certain that the reopening of parliament will take place in a good climate."
Parliament was reopening on Monday, and Juppe has set a confidence vote for the first day of the sessionm in an effort to unite the fractious coalition behind him .
